methods.label: Check the degree and discriminant
methods.explanation:
The coefficient of \(x^2\) depends on \(K\), so we must check when it vanishes before using the quadratic discriminant. If \(K=0\), the original equation becomes \(x=0\), which has a real solution.

For \(K\ne0\), expand and collect terms:
\[
K^2x^2-(3K^2+1)x+2K^2=0.
\]
Since the leading coefficient \(K^2\) is nonzero, this is a quadratic equation. We only need to determine whether its roots are real, so calculate its discriminant:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Delta&=(3K^2+1)^2-4(K^2)(2K^2)\\
&=K^4+6K^2+1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Even powers of real numbers are nonnegative, so \(\Delta\ge1>0\). A positive discriminant gives two distinct real roots. Thus every nonzero real \(K\) qualifies, and the separate case \(K=0\) qualifies as well. The answer is \(\boxed{\text{all real }K}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
